evals.expected_output: Should flag first, as the most serious defects: (1) `events` is written as an array of `{ name, ... }` objects on both 'pending' and 'shipping' -- it must be a Record keyed by event name (e.g. `events: { SubmitOrder: { targetState: 'processing', ... } }`); this doesn't type-check against WorkflowDefinition, and forced through (`as any`/plain JS) the validator accepts it with events named '0' and '1', so triggerEvent('submit_order') throws InvalidEventError; (2) `commands` are bare strings (`['validateOrder', 'chargePayment']`, `['assignWarehouse']`, `['sendConfirmation']`) -- each must be an object ref `{ name: 'validateOrder' }`, otherwise there is no `name` to resolve against the command registry. Then: (3) the submit_order event has commands (chargePayment can fail) but no errorState -- a `{ ok: false }` throws CommandFailureError and rolls back; (4) chargePayment likely needs idempotency keys since it's a payment command; (5) the 'failed' state has no events -- verify it is intentionally terminal. Should NOT flag the 'processing' state as able to get stuck or as needing a timeout: it is an onEnter gateway with targetState + errorState, so an instance passes through it in the same transaction and never rests there. Should NOT flag false positives on the valid timeout or onEnter patterns.

Should flag: (1) new Date().toISOString() instead of ctx.now.toISOString() — non-deterministic, (2) ctx.metadata.refundStatus = 'completed' — metadata is deepFreeze'd, so under strict mode (ESM modules and class bodies, which this command is) the assignment throws TypeError; only in non-strict code would it be silently ignored. Either way it's a bug — write to ctx.context instead, (3) catch block returns { ok: true } on Stripe error — hides infrastructure failure, refund may not have happened but workflow proceeds as if it did, (4) processRefund has no idempotency guard — if transaction rolls back and event re-fires, duplicate refund. sendRefundNotification is OK to return ok:true on failure (non-critical side effect) but should note the email service error isn't caught.

Should flag at least these v1.0.0 issues: (1) `observers: [...]` at the top level of WorkflowModule.forRootAsync — that field was REMOVED in v1.0.0; observers must be returned from useFactory as part of WorkflowModuleFactoryConfig. (2) The observer is being constructed with `new OrderAuditObserver()` rather than being a NestJS provider, which means it can't inject services like InvoiceService — and the observer body uses `this.invoiceService` which would be undefined. Recommend an OrderObserversModule that provides+exports the observer, then `imports: [OrderObserversModule]` in forRootAsync. (3) OrderAuditObserver.onEnter calls invoiceService.generateAndSend — that's BUSINESS-CRITICAL work in an observer. Observers are post-commit + at-most-once + error-contained. If the invoice send fails or the process crashes between commit and the observer firing, the invoice is silently lost. Move generateAndSend into a workflow command that runs inside the transaction. (4) SendThankYouEmailCommand catches the error and returns ok:true — that's the v0.x anti-pattern. In v1.0.0 the right fix is `readonly bestEffort = true;` on the class so the failure is recorded honestly while still allowing the chain to continue. (5) BONUS: forRootAsync isn't using the generic form — `forRootAsync<[pg.Pool]>` would typecheck the inject tokens against factory args. Should NOT recommend Math.random or any fix not in the v1.0.0 reviewer skill.

Should flag: (1) the definition adds a new event (RequestRefund) to the shipped state — a content change — but `version` stayed at 3; this makes WorkflowRuntime.initialize() throw WorkflowDefinitionError on the next deploy (content-hash mismatch for a known version), failing NestJS startup. `version` must bump to 4. (2) makeOrderInstance's returned object is missing `definitionVersion`, a required field on WorkflowInstance as of v5.0.0 — this either fails to typecheck or, if the type-check is being bypassed, silently produces fixtures with `definitionVersion` undefined at runtime; add a default like `definitionVersion: 1` (with `null` reserved for a fixture deliberately modeling a legacy pre-versioning row) so callers aren't forced to supply it via `overrides` every time. Should NOT flag the RequestRefund event's shape itself (targetState + commands) — that's a valid standard transition.

evals.prompt: Review an idempotency change that caches results outside the workflow transaction, uses a fresh UUID for every webhook retry, hashes arbitrary subjects implicitly, and reruns observers on replay. It also adds the new table as a required Kysely type member. Explain the defects and compatible corrections.
evals.expected_output: Use stable occurrence keys scoped to an instance; optional caller fingerprints compare exactly including presence. Enable optional transactional storage with idempotency:true after migration 007; preserve unkeyed calls and existing Kysely types. Replay committed success, routed failure, and guard rejection without commands, guards, observers or writes; outer rollback removes receipts. Same-key transaction-local recursion fails. Keyed results are JSON snapshots. Test real concurrent commit/rollback and do not claim exactly-once external effects or automatic pruning.
